mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate above 5.0% signals economic weakness and reduced corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint rise in housing starts and industrial production (both above their 3-month moving average) signals a robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both above 3-month moving average
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and INDPRO are above their 3-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (when the federal funds rate is rising), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during monetary tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls above 100,000 per month indicates a strengthening labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 600,000 units signals a weakening housing market and reduced economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 600.0.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 2.0% year-over-year and the federal funds rate remains below 0.5%, the market perceives accommodative monetary policy as sufficient to manage inflation, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.0% and FEDFUNDS <= 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: During supply contractions (when industrial production falls below its 3-month moving average), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced economic output and corporate production.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during supply contractions.
